newsitem.title: PERU: President Fujimori welcomes freed hostages.
newsitem.headline: President Fujimori welcomes freed hostages.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori greeted 225 freed hostages in person at the police hospital in Lima on Sunday night after their release from the Japanese ambassador's residence where they were held by Marxist guerrillas.

Fujimori, together with his daughter and first lady Keiko Sofia Fujimori spent 20 minutes with the released captives before returning to Government Palace. The worried-looking president left without speaking to reporters.
Keiko Sofia was named first lady of Peru in 1994 after Fujimori's separation from his former wife Susana Higuchi.
Also present at the hospital, Higuchi told reporters her former husband was concerned about his brother Pedro Fujimori, who was among the remaining hostages.
"The president of the republic is worried that his brother Pedro Fujimori was not freed. This is a rather lamentable occurrence," Higuchi said.
Surrounded by bodyguards, Fujimori looked worn and serious as he left the hospital.

Hundreds of journalists, family members and onlookers, many cheering or waving Peruvian flags, gathered outside the hospital to watch the hostages arrive and then start leaving one by one to return to their homes.
